samples.summary: Slides PUT validator leaves `themes[]` and `masters[]` completely unvalidated, allowing a stored payload that crashes every renderer/exporter of the deck
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlidesBody` only checks that `themes`/`masters` are arrays (line 472-478) and then walks `slides` and `layouts`. `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:102-103) assigns `root.themes = document.themes; root.masters = document.masters;` verbatim, so a `PUT` of `{meta:{title:'t',themeId:'t',masterId:'m'}, themes:[{}], masters:[{id:'m',themeId:'t',background:{fill:'red'}}], layouts:[], slides:[]}` returns 200 and is persisted. Downstream every consumer dereferences these unconditionally: `themeToXml` does `theme.colors[role]` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:97) and `escapeXmlAttr(theme.fonts.heading)` (theme.ts:103) -> TypeError when `colors`/`fonts` are absent; `resolveColor` does `theme.colors[color.role]` in the canvas paint path (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:105); `fillXml(master.background.fill)` -> `colorChildXml('red')` executes `'lumMod' in c` on a string primitive (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:57) which throws `TypeError: Cannot use 'in' operator`. Attacker = any workspace member or scoped API key (WorkspaceScopeGuard only asserts membership, no role). Result is a persistent denial of service: the deck no longer renders or exports for any viewer, and only another PUT can undo it. The inline comment at lines 489-492 justifies skipping `masters` on the grounds that a Master carries no `Block`s — true, but the fields that crash consumers are `background.fill` and `placeholderStyles`, not blocks, so the stated reason does not cover the hole the walk leaves open.

samples.summary: `escapeXmlAttr` assumes a string; several OOXML sinks pass unvalidated persisted values, turning a stored non-string into a TypeError that breaks export for the whole deck
samples.evidence: `escapeXmlAttr(s)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/xml.ts:5) calls `s.replace(...)` directly, unlike the sibling `attr()` helper on line 17 which does `String(value)` first. The hardening pass in this diff coerced the *numeric* animation attributes through `toXmlInt` but left the string ones raw: `escapeXmlAttr(presetClass)` where `presetClass = anim.pptxPreset.class` (animation.ts:217/257) and `escapeXmlAttr(anim.motionPath)` (animation.ts:245). `slide.animations` is never walked by `assertValidSlidesBody`, so a caller can `PUT` `{animations:[{pptxPreset:{class:1,id:1}}]}` and every subsequent `exportPptx` of that deck throws. The same shape applies to `escapeXmlAttr(el.id)` in shape.ts:209 / group.ts:102 / connector.ts:114 for *group children*, which the new `assertValidNestedElement` deliberately does not type-check (docs-content.controller.ts:595-600), and to `escapeXmlAttr(theme.fonts.heading)` (theme.ts:103). Availability impact only — no injection, since a string that does reach the sink is escaped.

samples.summary: Docs arm still uses `typeof x === 'object'` for `style` / inline `style`, which accepts an array; the slides arm added the `Array.isArray` rejection but the docs arm was not updated
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` line 371 (`!b.style || typeof b.style !== 'object'`) and line 437 (inline style) let an array through, because `typeof [] === 'object'`. The slides walk added exactly this check three lines apart in the same file — `assertValidSlideBlocks` line 715 rejects `typeof block.style !== 'object' || Array.isArray(block.style)` — and the branch's own lessons file (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md) calls out `typeof [] === 'object'` as the bug pattern. Consequence is limited (the block-style codec reads only named keys off the array, yielding `{}`), so this is a hardening inconsistency rather than an exploit, but it makes the docs arm advertise a shape guarantee it does not enforce.

samples.summary: `MIME_TO_EXT[mime]` is an un-hardened object-literal lookup keyed by an attacker-influenceable Content-Type, and its result reaches an unescaped `Target=` attribute and a zip entry path
samples.evidence: `deriveExt` (docx-exporter.ts:24-27) does `MIME_TO_EXT[blob.type.toLowerCase()] || 'bin'`. `blob.type` is the `Content-Type` header of a fetch against `inline.style.image.src`, i.e. attacker-controlled when a document points at an attacker's host. Lowercase prototype keys `constructor` and `__proto__` resolve through the prototype chain and are stringified into `media/image_N.<ext>` (line 61), which is then interpolated unescaped into `Target="${e.path}"` at lines 132 and 395. The stringified prototype members contain no `"`, so this is not an attribute break today — but it is precisely the `Record`-keyed-by-untrusted-data pattern this change swept everywhere else (see the diff's own note in the lessons doc), and the `Target` attribute has no escaping at all as a backstop.

samples.summary: The import-side mirror of the newly hardened role lookup is still an object literal keyed by an attribute out of an uploaded PPTX
samples.evidence: This change converted the export lookup to `SCHEME_BY_ROLE = new Map(...)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:28) specifically because `role` is untrusted. The inverse table `SCHEME_TO_ROLE: Record<string, ColorRole>` (import/pptx/color.ts:23) is read as `SCHEME_TO_ROLE[mapped]` at line 101, where `mapped` comes from a `<a:schemeClr val>` attribute in a user-uploaded .pptx. `val="constructor"` yields the `Object` constructor as the `role`, `val="__proto__"` yields `Object.prototype`; both are then persisted into the model as `{ kind: 'role', role: <non-string> }`. The export side now degrades that to black, so I could not complete an injection chain, but the un-normalized value flows into the CRDT and into `theme.colors[role]` lookups on the render path.

samples.summary: New group-children walk recurses without a depth bound, so a deeply nested PUT body can exhaust the stack inside the validator
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` recurses `data.children` -> `assertValidNestedElement` -> `assertValidElementData` (lines 636-641) with no depth cap, and `assertValidBlock` recurses through nested table cells the same way. `JSON_BODY_LIMIT` in packages/backend/src/main.ts:49 is a large limit (the comment references 25MB content-import routes), so a body of ~40-byte nested `{"type":"group","data":{"children":[` frames reaches hundreds of thousands of levels. A RangeError inside the handler is caught by Nest and returned as a 500 rather than crashing the process, and V8's own `JSON.parse` may reject the payload first, which is why confidence is low — but the recursion path is newly introduced here and unbounded.

verdict.reason: The validation gap is real as described (assertValidSlidesBody checks only that themes/masters are arrays at docs-content.controller.ts:472-478 and skips the masters walk per the comment at :490-492; writeSlidesRoot persists them verbatim at slides-tree.ts:102-103), but it is not a Security-lane blocker. (1) No trust boundary is crossed: WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-36) admits only authenticated workspace members or workspace-scoped API keys, i.e. actors already authorized to destructively replace the entire deck (slides-tree.ts:86-92) — a schema-valid PUT of {slides:[],layouts:[]} produces equivalent viewer-facing loss, so there is no escalation, IDOR, or unauthenticated reach. (2) The proposed validation would not prevent the claimed DoS: getActiveTheme (view/canvas/render-context.ts:88-96) intentionally throws whenever meta.themeId does not match an entry in doc.themes, which is reachable with perfectly well-formed Theme objects plus a validated non-empty mismatched themeId — the breakage is a documented "programmer error" design choice, not a security control. (3) The injection sinks are already hardened by construction: export/pptx/theme.ts:92,103-104 escapes name/typefaces with escapeXmlAttr and normalizes colors via toSrgbHex (:95-97), and export/pptx/color.ts:39-50,62-78 coerces modifiers to finite numbers, maps roles through a closed table, and normalizes hex to [0-9A-F]{6} with a black fallback — so attacker-chosen theme content cannot inject XML; the worst case is a TypeError. (4) The impact is client-side only: no file under packages/backend imports @wafflebase/slides and no exportPptx/exportPdf/renderSlide reference exists there, so the API process cannot be crashed. The residual issue is missing input robustness causing a client exception, which the rubric assigns to the correctness lens ("general logic bugs"), not to authorization, secrets, injection, crypto, SSRF, deserialization, or path traversal.
